# kmtest conformance baseline — parse_kmtest_serial.py format
# arch=i386  generated by `vibeos-cli conformance --arch i386 --write-baseline`
# 2026-10-16: ObTypes 773/9 -> 763/19, LOWERED BY DESIGN (x3 sweeps, all three arches alike). The
#   Process, Thread and Job types now carry the Windows 11 masks measured on real hardware
#   (process R/W/X/A 0x20410/0x20bea/0x121001/0x1fffff, thread 0x20048/0x20437/0x121800/0x1fffff,
#   job GenericAll and ValidAccessMask 0x1f003f): the NT5 ValidAccessMask silently stripped the
#   *_LIMITED_INFORMATION rights from every handle, so NtGetNextThread with a LIMITED right failed
#   ACCESS_DENIED. ObTypes.cpp picks its expectations by NtDdiVersion, and we still report 5.2, so
#   266-268 compare against the 2003 masks: 10 checks (4 process, 4 thread, 2 job). At the version
#   flip they take the test's Vista column instead, which still differs from Windows 11 in thread
#   GenericExecute (+THREAD_RESUME 0x1000) and job (+JOB_OBJECT_IMPERSONATE 0x20); give the test
#   a Windows 10 column then.
# 2026-10-16b (x2 byte-identical sweeps, all three arches): FsRtlExpression 258/8 -> 266/0
#   (FsRtlIsDbcsInExpression broke out of its name loop before taking the match count, so a
#   trailing `*`/DOS_STAR/DOS_DOT match on the end-of-name pass was dropped); KeDeviceQueue
#   44/1 -> 45/0 (Type was the literal 7, GateObject; DeviceQueueObject is 20); SeInheritance
#   704433/14 -> 704447/0 (SeAssignSecurityEx no longer writes its output before the faults the
#   test provokes; mandatory label ACEs inherit by the ordinary rules); HidPDescription 28/9 ->
#   33/4 (the description is zeroed before parsing; no ID byte on a report type that is absent;
#   LEFT: one ReportIDs entry per collection with ReportID = Index, the C's FIXME, and
#   PreparsedDataLength in our layout, not Windows'); ObTypes 763/19 -> 768/14 is upstream-sync's
#   test column (32c69eb0b10), not this lane; 7 new tests banked (EtwActivity, EtwProvider,
#   ExPool2, FeatureConfig, MmMapIoSpaceEx, RtlUtf8, and MmReservedMappingFixed, below).
#   ZwMapViewOfSection: ROS views honour ZeroBits with no base, refuse a commit larger than the
#   view and a reservation of a read-only section; ARM3 says INVALID_PARAMETER_9 for a reserve
#   of a section with no file. LEFT (owed): 211, a reserved view past the end of the file. Do
#   NOT just drop the size check for it: that let a view outrun the segment, and unmapping it
#   corrupted the file's cached pages (later reads wrong, BUGCHECK 0x1E on x86).
#   EXPECTED, re-checked against the win11-amd64 column (Windows passes them by another branch,
#   not by being right where we are wrong): ExDoubleList, NpfsFileInfo (both pick their
#   expectation by PRCB_BUILD_DEBUG; we are checked, Windows 11 is free) and MmSection 14 (its
#   WS03 column; we report 5.2).
#   i386: HalSystemInfo 88/1 -> 89/0 (the PCI config handler refuses a port outside its
#   range). ZwMapViewOfSection 128/6 -> 132/2; 181 owed: i386 NtMapViewOfSection refuses ZeroBits
#   21 as INVALID_PARAMETER_4 where Windows answers NO_MEMORY. MmReservedMapping 187/44 is a TEST BUG kept as an
#   expected failure: its ReactOS branch expects the PAE MMPTE_LIST (<<32) and this kernel is
#   non-PAE (<<12); MmReservedMappingFixed (same source, corrected) is 231/0. ExInterlocked
#   296/297 is the test's own SaveState (its TODO: inline asm around a C call); the export
#   preserves edi. KeSpinLock 30 is owed: the queued spinlocks are the C's plain-lock HACK.
# 2026-10-15: RtlRangeList pass 521 -> 520: upstream 09a03ec307d deleted one RtlFindRange check.
#   ZwAllocateVirtualMemory unchanged (269/2): upstream's StressTesting rewrite keeps 1024 x 5 MB here.
# 2026-10-12: ZwAllocateVirtualMemory pass 258 -> 269, fail 2 (same assertion, now line 145). Upstream's test sync renumbered it (147->145,
#   512->613); NtAllocateVirtualMemory now takes ZeroBits as NT does (a 32-bit limit, clamped to
#   the VAD ceiling) instead of failing INVALID_PARAMETER_3, clearing the ZERO BITS rows. Left:
#   145 MEM_PHYSICAL|MEM_RESERVE, and on 64-bit 613: reserving charges no page-table commit
#   (roadmap known bugs). The x64 stress is capped at 4096 chunks (linear VAD search).
# 2026-10-11 (x2 sweeps, identical): ZwAllocateVirtualMemory pass 849 -> 258, LOWERED BY DESIGN.
#   Commit is now accounted (ARM3/commit.rs, no pagefile), so the MEM_COMMIT stress loops end at
#   the commit limit; the test takes their every-tenth-chunk read/write checks on the first 50
#   chunks only (the count no longer depends on RAM), and accepts STATUS_COMMITMENT_LIMIT as the
#   exhaustion status. The dropped passes were repeats of the same check on more chunks.
# 2026-10-11 (x2 identical sweeps, all three arches alike): IoReadWrite 16192/151 -> 15563/0:
#   NtReadFile probed its buffer with the range-only probe_user_buffer where the C has
#   ProbeForWrite, so a NULL buffer reached the test driver as an IRP; the 119 kernel call sites that
#   translated a write probe that way now use probe_user_buffer_write. The pass count FALLS
#   because those calls now fail before the driver, whose per-IRP assertions no longer run.
#   MmSection 337/30 -> 353/14: SectionOffset rounds down in place and grows ViewSize (the
#   unaligned \Device\PhysicalMemory view), and a caller-supplied FileObject always gets a data
#   section as on Server 2003. The 14 left are one cascade: on 2003 closing a file's last handle
#   tears down its data segment, so a later section re-references the new file object (count
#   4); our segment outlives the close and keeps the old one (count 3). ZwCreateSection 4 -> 3:
#   SEC_LARGE_PAGES returns STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER_6, as the C does.
#   ZwMapViewOfSection 127/7 -> 128/6, now level with amd64 and arm64.
# 2026-10-11b (x2 identical sweeps): ExSingleList 240/12 -> 252/0 and ExDoubleList 130/16 ->
#   {i386 146/0, 64-bit 138/8}: the interlocked list removes poison the freed entry under the C's
#   `#if DBG`, which the Rust had behind cfg(debug_assertions) (never set in our release-built
#   kernel crates, while this tree runs DBG=1). NpfsFileInfo 50/25 -> 56/19: IndexNumber is now
#   nonzero and the name accounting charges FIELD_OFFSET(FileName), not sizeof, with the full
#   FileNameLength on overflow. ObTypes 767/15 -> 773/9: DebugObject, Profile and WmiGuid access
#   masks restored to their header values; Desktop now keeps handle counts.
#   EXPECTED leftovers: NpfsFileInfo's 19 are its sizeof-4 query, which a checked build fails
#   INFO_LENGTH_MISMATCH before npfs, as Windows does; the test lacks the KmtIsCheckedBuild guard
#   its IoFilesystem sibling has (see NtQueryInformationFile). ObTypes' 9: WindowStation cannot
#   keep handle counts with no Open/Close procedure (win32k supplies them on Windows); Port's
#   InvalidAttributes 0x7b2 is valid 2003 SP2 RTM per the test's own comment; the two Filter*
#   types need fltmgr, which this sweep does not load.
# 2026-10-10 (x2 identical sweeps): x86 conformance now boots the WRITABLE root on i386 too
#   (livecd-rw.iso). IoFilesystem 162/142 -> 358/3, MmSection 79/11 -> 337/30, ZwCreateSection
#   4/3 -> 283/4, IoCreateFile 45/8 -> 106/7, ZwMapViewOfSection 109/18 -> 127/7: the tests
#   now run instead of bailing on read-only CDFS. Every newly reached failing assertion is one
#   amd64 already has. Getting here fixed fastfat's flush (a stdcall view of a cdecl helper
#   returned FatCommonFlushBuffers' finally into its stack) and ExReturnPoolQuota on special pool.
# 2026-10-09 (x2 sweeps): MmSection 13->11 (PAGE_NOCACHE was missing from the Rust
#   PAGE_FLAGS_VALID_FOR_SECTION). ExResource/KdSystemDebugControl/FindFile/NtCreateSection/
#   ZwMapViewOfSection gains came from master, banked here. RtlCaptureContextKM/UM rows dropped:
#   amd64-only (testlist #ifdef), they read NO-END.
# 2026-10-08: +RtlSplayTreeKM 139/0, +SeTokenFiltering 11/0, RtlSplayTree NO-END -> 139/0.
#   generictable under-sized every node by 4 bytes on i386 (the 8-aligned UserData offset is 24,
#   not the 20-byte link sum), which fixed both splay rows; token filtering's group loop never
#   advanced. RtlException stays quarantined: clang's x86-32 try-level limit, see the list.
# KeSpinLock re-seeded 2026-08-02, 710/75 -> 753/32 — a REAL FIX, not a re-roll, and it
#   landed on the UP kernel even though the bug was found chasing an MP one. hal-rust's x86
#   Kx{Acquire,Release}SpinLock were hard-coded to the UP arm of spinlock.h AND to
#   KI_TRACK_SPINLOCK_OWNER=0, but that macro is plain `#if DBG`: the C half stamps and
#   clears the owner on every checked build, UP included. So ntoskrnl stamped locks that the
#   HAL never cleared. Both now delegate to ntkrnl_sys::inline::ke — one implementation, per
#   spinlock.h's own "the two MUST agree". Was 75 here where amd64/arm64 sit at 2, because
#   i386 is the only arch whose Ke*SpinLock* come from hal.spec rather than ntoskrnl.spec.
#   Residual 32 = upstream's queued-spinlock HACK + the try-acquire owner stamp; see the
#   matching note in kmtest-smp2.txt.
# KeEvent re-seeded 2026-09-12, 42733 -> 42601, by HAND and deliberately NOT by
#   `--write-baseline`. The MP kernel became the default boot that day, and
#   KeEvent.c:85 excludes its `Wait=TRUE` block when KmtIsMultiProcessorBuild is
#   true (the test's manual cleanup would leave the MP dispatcher lock held). The
#   delta is arithmetic, not a sample: 3 IRQLs x 2 event types x 2 operations x 11
#   assertions in CheckEvent = 132, exactly, and all three arches report the same
#   42601. A wholesale re-seed was tried first and REVERTED -- it re-rolls every
#   row from one sweep, which collapsed 5 `assert?` bistable marks into `assert`
#   (freezing one boot's face into the floor, the thing `--only` exists to
#   prevent) and deleted this file's own provenance comments. Prefer a hand edit
#   with a reason over a wholesale rewrite whenever the change is understood.
# 2026-10-08, by HAND (rows only, per-arch samples all identical): banked a month of
#   unbanked gains -- ExHardError 24/6 -> 30/0, IoVolume 1 -> 7 (ExResource stays 845 on purpose,
#   c92ea2a: 879 minus the 34 checks its race can cost),
#   ObSecurity 694 -> 695, RtlRangeList -> 5xx and the rest below. IoDeviceObject
#   stays 184: 185 twice, then 184 in the validation sweep -- bistable, not banked. And ObTypes is now a
#   .cpp (upstream, synced 2026-09-21): the parser only matched `<file>.c:<line>`, so its
#   identities had silently vanished from every sweep since. The row now carries the
#   ObTypes.cpp identities -- a rename plus two newly-passing asserts, not new failures.
# 2026-10-08 (later), by HAND, two agreeing sweeps: MmMapLockedPagesSpecifyCache and
#   MmReservedMapping come out of quarantine after their kernel bugs were fixed (see the
#   sweep list). MmReservedMapping's 44 are the TEST's i386 expectation, not ours: it wants
#   the size PTE at `(TotalPtes + 2) << 32`, a value no 32-bit non-PAE PTE can hold. We
#   store it in u.List.NextEntry at bit 12 (0x3000), exactly as upstream's C does, so
#   upstream ReactOS fails these same lines; the ValidateMapping FALSEs cascade from :159.
